lessons.bigQuestion: A footballer practises the same basics every day. What are the 'basics' of good recitation, and why practise them again in Year 7?
objectives: To understand how recitation is assessed in Key Stage 3 and to set a personal hifdh and tajweed goal for the year

hook.text: A footballer practises the same basics every day. What are the 'basics' of good recitation, and why practise them again in Year 7?
hook.a: Correct makharij, sifat and rules: in Key Stage 3 we move from knowing rules to using them without thinking.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it' (Bukhari).

teach.note: Each pupil has their induction-week placement in the portal. Year 7 minimum: 'Abasa, An-Nazi'at and An-Naba' (80 to 78), completing Juz' 'Amma.

teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

practice.q: Score this example against the rubric: a pupil recites Al-Fatihah fluently but says ٱلْحَمْدُ with a 'h' instead of ح.
practice.a: Hifdh 4; makharij 2 (ح said as ه); rules 4; fluency 4; target: ح from the middle of the throat.
practice.model: I do: hifdh: no prompts, 4. Makharij: ح became ه, which changes the letter, so 2. Rules and fluency fine, 4. One target: say ح from the middle of the throat.

practice.q: Year 7 hifdh minimum completes ...
practice.a: Juz' 'Amma

independent.q: In the portal response box, write your hifdh target, one tajweed target and your weekly revision plan (sabaq, sabqi, manzil). Today's rota group recites Al-Fatihah and one short surah.
independent.a: A realistic plan: e.g. sabaq 'Abasa 1 to 8; sabqi last week's ayat; manzil 114 to 100 over the week.
independent.model: The teacher models a plan: 'Sabaq: 'Abasa 1 to 8 this week. Sabqi: revise Monday's ayat each day. Manzil: two short surahs a day from 114 down.'

independent.q: Extend: choose the time of day you will revise and why.
independent.a: For example: after Fajr, when the mind is fresh.

independent.q: Stretch: explain why revising old surahs matters as much as learning new ones.
independent.a: Memorised Qur'an escapes without revision (Bukhari and Muslim: it escapes faster than camels from their hobbles).

exit.q: New ayat for today are called ...
exit.a: sabaq

exit.q: Back to our ponder: A footballer practises the same basics every day. What are the 'basics' of good recitation, and why practise them again in Year 7?
exit.a: Correct makharij, sifat and rules: in Key Stage 3 we move from knowing rules to using them without thinking.

practice.a: ه: deepest part of the throat; خ: part nearest the mouth.
practice.model: I do: وَ: lips. هُ: deepest part of the throat, near the chest. وَ: lips. يَ: middle of the tongue. خْ: upper throat, near the mouth, heavy. شَىٰ: middle of the tongue, then the alif from the jawf.

independent.q: Extend: write a pair of words where ع and ء change the meaning.
independent.a: عَلِيم (all-knowing) and أَلِيم (painful).

independent.q: Stretch: why are throat letters the izhar letters for noon sakinah?
independent.a: They are far from the tongue tip where noon is made, so the noon stays clear.

exit.q: خ is made ...
exit.a: in the throat, nearest the mouth

lessons.bigQuestion: The tongue makes 18 of the 28 letters. Why might Allah have given such a small muscle so much work?

hook.text: The tongue makes 18 of the 28 letters. Why might Allah have given such a small muscle so much work?

check.q: Which letter is made with the side of the tongue?
check.why: ض alone is from the side. ظ is the tip on the edge of the top teeth; ط the tip on the roots.

practice.q: Read «أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰٓ» (80:4) and name the makhraj of each ذ and ك.
practice.a: ذ: tip on the edge of the top teeth; ك: back of the tongue (a little forward of ق).
practice.model: I do: يَذَّ: tongue tip peeps to the edge of the top teeth, doubled. كَّ: back of tongue, doubled. ٱلذِّكْرَىٰٓ: same ذ, then ك, then stretch.

practice.q: Whistling letters?
practice.a: ص ز س

independent.q: Makharij audit (pupil PDF): for 80:9 to 16, label each tongue letter with its point. Today's rota group recites 80:1 to 8.
independent.a: e.g. ش يَخْشَىٰ middle; ل تَلَهَّىٰ edge to tip; ك كَلَّآ back; ذ تَذْكِرَةٌ tip and top teeth edge; ص صُحُفٍ whistle; ط مُّطَهَّرَةٍ tip and roots; ر بَرَرَةٍ tip with gum.
independent.model: The teacher labels the first: ش in يَخْشَىٰ, middle of the tongue.

independent.q: Extend: say three pairs that are often confused and the difference.
independent.a: ث/س: peeps out vs whistle; ذ/ز; ظ/ض: tip vs side.

independent.q: Stretch: why is Arabic called 'the language of the daad'?
independent.a: ض is a sound few other languages have, so Arabic is named after it.

exit.q: ث is made ...
exit.a: with the tongue tip on the edge of the top teeth
options: with the tongue tip on the edge of the top teeth
with the side of the tongue

exit.q: Back to our ponder: The tongue makes 18 of the 28 letters. Why might Allah have given such a small muscle so much work?
exit.a: It is a sign of Allah's design; we thank Him by using the tongue for good speech and His words.

independent.model: The teacher finds the first: ز in وَزَيْتُونًۭا (80:29), safeer.

independent.q: Extend: write the three safeer letters.
independent.a: ص ز س

independent.q: Stretch: why is takrir described but avoided in practice?
independent.a: Raa naturally tends to roll; reciters keep one tap so no extra raa is added.

exit.q: Safeer letters?
exit.a: ص ز س

hook.text: Raa and laam are light letters, yet sometimes we say them heavy. How can one letter be both?
hook.a: They are not isti'la letters, so their weight depends on the vowels around them.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them' (Al-A'raf 7:180). The laam in His Name is said with care.

starter.a: و or ي sakin after fathah

teach.heading: Raa with sukoon: look before it
bullets: But heavy if an isti'la letter follows in the word (مِرْصَادًا)
teach.note: تَرْهَقُهَا is 80:41. فِرْعَوْنَ is 79:17; مِرْصَادًا is 78:21; ٱرْجِعِىٓ is 89:28: all in Juz' 'Amma.

teach.heading: The laam in the Name Allah

practice.model: I do: فَأَقْبَرَهُۥ: the raa has fathah, heavy. ٱمْرِئٍ: the raa has kasrah, light. فِرْعَوْنَ: raa sakinah, before it ف with kasrah, and no isti'la letter after it in the word, so light.

independent.model: The teacher marks the first: ٱلْمَرْءُ (80:34): raa sakinah after fathah, heavy.

independent.a: Heavy both times (112:1 after fathah; 112:2 starting).

independent.q: Stretch: why is the raa in مِرْصَادًا heavy, though a kasrah comes before?
independent.a: An isti'la letter (ص) follows the raa in the same word.

exit.q: Raa with kasrah is ...
exit.a: light

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Raa and laam are light letters, yet sometimes we say them heavy. How can one letter be both?

lessons.title: Madd 1: the two families
objectives: Define madd asli and madd far'i
Identify the cause of madd
Sort madd by cause

keywords.def: secondary madd, longer because of a hamza or sukoon

starter: How many counts is natural madd?
Give a word with madd muttasil.

teach.heading: The two families
bullets: Far'i: caused by hamza or sukoon
teach.note: Draw a family tree with two branches. Explain that far'i builds on the natural madd and adds length for a reason. Ask: what are the two causes?

teach.heading: Cause: hamza
teach.note: Examples: السَّمَاءِ (muttasil), يَا أَيُّهَا (munfasil), آمَنُوا (badal). Pupils decide the cause in each. Revise the counts and remind that consistent length matters.

teach.heading: Cause: sukoon
bullets: Leen: waaw or yaa sakin, 2-6 when stopping
teach.note: Examples: الضَّالِّينَ (lazim), الْعَالَمِينَ stopped (arid), خَوْفٍ (leen). Pupils explain why each is longer than natural.

teach.heading: Sort and justify
teach.note: Use a sorting task with 12 words. Pupils justify each answer. Give feedback on reasoning, not only counts.

practice: Give the cause of madd lazim.
independent: Sort 15 words on a table: type, cause, counts
Mark the madd in Al-Fatihah and Quraysh
exit: Name the two causes of far'i madd.
Which madd is always six counts?
lessons.homework: Mark every madd in Surat Al-Fil and note its type and counts.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: flow chart for deciding madd type. Stretch: explain why lazim is longer than 'arid.

lessons.title: Madd 2: madd lazim in detail
objectives: Name the four types of madd lazim
Identify each type in the mushaf
Read each at six counts

keywords.def: in the name of a letter

starter: Give the counts for madd lazim.
Name a word with lazim from Al-Fatihah.

teach.heading: Four types
teach.note: Draw a 2x2 table: word or letter vs shaddah or sukoon. All four types are six counts. Ask: what do kalimi and harfi refer to?

teach.heading: Kalimi
bullets: Madd letter followed by shaddah or sukoon in the same word
teach.note: The mukhaffaf kalimi is rare and appears in آلْآنَ. Pupils read each example at six counts. Check the shaddah and sukoon.

teach.heading: Harfi
bullets: Letters at the start of some surahs
teach.note: Harfi occurs in the opening letters: pupils meet الم at the start of Al-Baqarah and ن at the start of Al-Qalam. The name of the letter is spelt out, e.g. لام and ميم, and that is why they are stretched. Present the principle; teacher demonstrates.

teach.heading: Practice
bullets: Do not rush into the next letter
teach.note: Pairs: one recites, the other counts with fingers. Provide feedback. Close with a short recitation of الضَّالِّينَ with steady six-count madd.

practice: How many counts is madd lazim?
What is the difference between kalimi and harfi?

Create a flow chart for deciding madd lazim type
exit: Name the four types of madd lazim.

lessons.send: SEND/EAL: 2x2 table with examples. Stretch: find other letters at the start of surahs.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Qadr: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Al-Qadr accurately
Apply makharij, sifat and madd
Begin to memorise the surah
starter: Name the four types of madd lazim.

teach.heading: The surah
teach.note: Introduce the surah: Allah sent down the Qur'an on the Night of Decree. Chunk and echo. Rules: ghunnah in إِنَّا; ikhfa in أَنزَلْنَاهُ; laam qamariyyah in الْقَدْرِ.

teach.heading: Ayat 3-5
bullets: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ
teach.note: Meaning: the Night of Decree is better than a thousand months; angels and the Spirit descend by their Lord's permission with every decree; peace it is until the rise of dawn. Chunk and echo.

teach.heading: Tajweed
teach.note: Check: tanween in خَيْرٌ meets meem: idgham with ghunnah. The noon of مِن meets kaaf in كُلِّ: ikhfa. The meem sakinah of رَبِّهِم meets meem: idgham shafawi. The madd in الْمَلَائِكَةُ is muttasil. Pupils label rules on a printed text.

teach.heading: Learn it
teach.note: Memorise ayat 1-2 now; 3 at home. Use chaining and test aloud. Praise accuracy of rules as well as memory.

practice: Which rule is in خَيْرٌ مِّنْ؟
independent: Read Al-Qadr in pairs; label rules
exit: What is better than a thousand months?
Name one tajweed rule in ayah 3.
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Qadr daily and learn ayat 1-3 by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and text with rules highlighted. Stretch: learn the whole surah.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Qadr: meaning and reflection
objectives: Explain the main message of Al-Qadr
Use a simple method for tadabbur
Recite the whole surah from memory

keywords.def: reflecting deeply on the meaning of the Qur'an
the Night of Decree, in Ramadan

teach.heading: The message
bullets: The Qur'an was revealed on a blessed night
The night is better than a thousand months
teach.note: Ask the class what makes a time special. Explain that Allah has honoured this night, and that the sources indicate it is in Ramadan, in the last ten nights. Keep to what is established.

teach.heading: Questions to ask
bullets: What is said? The night is special
teach.note: Model a simple tadabbur method with these four questions. Use them on ayat 3-5. Ask for personal responses and acceptable answers.

teach.heading: Thinking about the Qur'an
bullets: كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ (38:29)
teach.note: Read these two ayat in meaning: do they not reflect upon the Qur'an; a blessed Book We sent down so they may ponder its verses. Link the two parts of the Qur'an's purpose: recite and think.

teach.heading: Putting it together
teach.note: Pupils recite Al-Qadr and complete a sentence: This surah teaches me ... so I will ... Share a few. Conclude with dua for the Night of Decree.

independent: Write answers to the four tadabbur questions
Write a short reflection of 5 sentences on Al-Qadr
exit: What does the surah say about the Night of Decree?
Why do we reflect on the Qur'an?
lessons.homework: Write a half-page reflection on Al-Qadr and recite it every day.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sentence frames for tadabbur. Stretch: compare Al-Qadr with the ayah 2:185.

lessons.title: Memorisation technique and recital assessment
objectives: Describe a good memorisation routine
Revise Al-Qadr, Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh
Complete a recital with the rubric
starter: Name the three parts of a revision plan.

teach.heading: A good routine
teach.note: Explain that memory improves through short, regular practice. Show a small weekly plan. Ask: what time of day is best for you?

teach.heading: Three layers
teach.note: Pupils plan a week using three layers. Show a sample. Notice that older surahs are revised weekly. Pupils may use a check-list.

teach.heading: Dealing with mistakes
bullets: Say the correct ayah five times
teach.note: Tell pupils that everyone forgets. Keep a list of difficult ayat. Do not give up. Encourage dua for strong memory and humility.

teach.heading: Recital
teach.note: Assess with the rubric from lesson 1. Provide one strength and one target. Compare with the baseline and celebrate progress.

practice: Name one of your goals from September.
independent: Complete a revision plan for the next four weeks
Recite your chosen surah for the rubric
Write a reflection comparing baseline and now
exit: Name two layers of a revision plan.
What is one target for next term?

lessons.send: SEND/EAL: revision planner with visual cues. Stretch: coach a partner in memorisation.

hook.text: A poor, blind man comes to ask about Islam while you are busy with important people. What would you do, and why?
hook.a: Allah taught that the sincere seeker deserves our full attention: worth is in the heart, not status (80:1 to 10).

islamicLink.text: These ayat were revealed about 'Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, a blind Companion who came to the Prophet ﷺ to learn while he was speaking to leaders of Quraysh (Tirmidhi). Allah teaches that the one who comes seeking and fearing Allah must be welcomed (Abasa 80:8 to 10).

bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: The Prophet frowned and turned away
Because there came to him the blind man, [interrupting].
But what would make you perceive, [O Muhammad], that perhaps he might be purified
Or be reminded and the remembrance would benefit him?
As for he who thinks himself without need,
And not upon you [is any blame] if he will not be purified.
But as for he who came to you striving [for knowledge]

quote.text: يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ ٱلْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ (٣٤) وَأُمِّهِۦ وَأَبِيهِ (٣٥) وَصَٰحِبَتِهِۦ وَبَنِيهِ (٣٦) لِكُلِّ ٱمْرِئٍۢ مِّنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ شَأْنٌۭ يُغْنِيهِ (٣٧) وُجُوهٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ مُّسْفِرَةٌۭ (٣٨) ضَاحِكَةٌۭ مُّسْتَبْشِرَةٌۭ (٣٩) وَوُجُوهٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌۭ (٤٠) تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ (٤١) أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْكَفَرَةُ ٱلْفَجَرَةُ (٤٢)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: On the Day a man will flee from his brother And his mother and his father
And his wife and his children, For every man, that Day, will be a matter adequate for him.
[Some] faces, that Day, will be bright - Laughing, rejoicing at good news.
And [other] faces, that Day, will have upon them dust. Blackness will cover them.
Those are the disbelievers, the wicked ones.

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 80:34-42 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Teacher recites one ayah (talaqqi)
Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: 80:38 to 39: bright, laughing, rejoicing. Dust is on the other faces (80:40).

practice.q: Chunk and link 'Abasa 80:34-42 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 80:34-42 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 80:34-42. Ayah 34: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 35 the same way. Then link: recite 34 and 35 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

practice.q: «يَوْمَئِذٍۢ شَأْنٌۭ» is ...
practice.a: ikhfa

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 80:34-42 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: In the portal box, contrast the two groups of faces in 80:38 to 42.
independent.a: Bright and joyful (believers) against dust-covered and darkened (the disbelieving, wicked).

independent.q: Recite the whole of 'Abasa (42 ayat).
independent.a: All 42 ayat with no more than three prompts.

exit.q: 'Abasa 80:39: «ضَاحِكَةٌۭ ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: مُّسْتَبْشِرَةٌۭ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: On the Day of Judgement a person runs from his brother, mother, father, wife and children (80:34 to 36). Why would anyone run from the people they love most?
exit.a: Each person will be busy with their own matter that Day (80:37). Only faith and good deeds help.
